title: Usage Commitments and Soft-Cap Transition Playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: This playbook defines product requirements, acceptance criteria, and operational runbook for introducing usage commitments (monthly reserved units) with an optional soft-cap transition window that gracefully shifts customers from soft-overage behavior into hard quota enforcement or paid overage. Goal: reduce billing surprises, increase predictable revenue, and provide clear UX + automated ops escalation for borderline consumption patterns. This document clarifies scope (what is in/out for MVP), how rate limits and per-route quotas map to commitments, expected pricing signals, and the billing acceptance criteria required before we flip the backend enforcement flag.
scope_clarification: MVP includes: definition of committed units per plan, soft-cap grace window behavior (configurable 0-14 days), per-route attribution for high-cost endpoints, invoice line-item for committed discounts, and automated notifications. Excludes: per-tenant credit exchange, settlement micro-optimizations, and marketplace partner billing flows (future work).
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Initial PRD drafted and reviewed with finance; high level pricing bands agreed.
2026-03-05: ENG spike completed to validate telemetry for per-route consumption; kernel-level cost tags available.
2026-03-09: Design mocking for console UX (commitment signup, soft-cap toggle, usage graph) shared with PM and Design.
2026-03-12: Legal reviewed terms for automatic overage billing; requested explicit opt-in language for EU customers.
2026-03-14: Implementation plan reviewed in cross-functional sync; ready for engineering backlog prioritization.
decision_log: Adopt percentage-based soft-cap notification thresholds: 80% (notice), 95% (actionable), 100% (soft overage starts).
Soft-cap window default: 7 days; configurable per account at enterprise tier.
Default transition behavior: after configured window expires, either (a) auto-bill overage or (b) enforce hard throttle based on account setting. Billing default = auto-bill.
Per-route cost attribution will use existing per-token cost weights; high-cost label applied to re-ranking and long-context routes.
Discount for commitments implemented as a contract-level percentage off on unit rate, applied at invoice time and visible in pricing preview.
Do not bundle soft-cap grace into free credits; separate line item on invoice for transparency (finance request).
tradeoffs: Option A (auto-bill after window) minimizes customer friction but increases potential disputes — requires stronger invoices and dispute tooling.
Option B (hard throttle) reduces surprise invoices but can severely degrade customer UX for high-value workflows.
We chose A for MVP with stronger notification cadence and an easy rollback path to throttle in edge cases.
Engineering complexity: per-route attribution increases cost of kcalculation but provides accurate unit economics for decision making.
review_feedback: Finance: require visible line-item for commitment discount and soft-overage charges in invoice preview.
Legal: require explicit consent checkbox for automatic billing on account settings; add EU-specific consumer language.
Design: add a 'what happens next' modal on reaching 95% with clear toggles to move to throttle or accept billing.
Reliability: recommend circuit-breaker threshold and fallback to lower-cost model variant if overage spike detected.
acceptance_criteria: Backend: committed_unit field supported on account object and persisted to billing pipeline (verified by API integration test).
Backend: soft-cap window and enforcement_mode flags configurable per-account via admin API.
Billing: discount line item for commitments appears on invoice and matches expected math for example account (finance validation).
Notifications: email + console banner generated at 80% and 95% thresholds with correct interpolated values and links to upgrade/change settings.
Observability: per-account usage heatmap available in Console for last 30 days and triggers a PagerDuty incident if delta > 3x baseline in 1h.
Rate Limiting: when enforcement_mode = throttle, Ratelimit headers reflect remaining tokens and are documented in API docs.
Edge cases: migrating existing free-tier customers to commitments preserves credits and shows pro-rated adjustment on first invoice.
Legal/Compliance: EU customers require explicit opt-in for auto-billing; system must persist opt-in flag and include terms link on invoice.
implementation_notes: API changes: PATCH /accounts/{id} supports committed_units, soft_cap_window_days, enforcement_mode.
Billing pipeline: apply commitment_discount_pct before calculating overage charges; ensure rounding parity with finance rules.
Telemetry: tag all usage events with commitment_id when applicable for accurate attribution.
Console: add 'Commitments' tab on Billing page with signup flow and preview calculator.
Migrations: backfill committed_units=null to 0; generate migration report for accounts with historical pre-pay credits.
test_plan: Unit tests for billing math covering combinations of discounts, pro-ration, and overage rounding.
Integration tests: simulate 30-day consumption pattern hitting thresholds to validate notifications and invoice content.
E2E QA: sign up commitment via console, trigger soft-overage, verify email flows and invoice line-items in staging billing exports.
Security: ensure committed_units and enforcement flags are authorized and cannot be escalated by non-admin users.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Beta, 2 weeks): invite top 10 pilot customers (existing enterprise accounts) to opt-in; monitor dispute rate and support load.
Phase 2 (Gradual, 4 weeks): open to all enterprise tier accounts; enable default soft-cap window of 7 days; finance on-call during billing runs.
Phase 3 (General Availability): enable self-serve for all paid plans and surface commitments in pricing calculator.
operational_playbook: If customer disputes auto-bill within 14 days, create billing dispute ticket and place temporary credit hold pending investigation.
On PagerDuty alert for usage spike, send proactive communication and offer temporary throttle or emergency credits per policy.
Rollback: admin flag to disable auto-billing globally for an account; requires manual audit and finance notification.
notes: Related: aligns with revenue predictability initiative (Q2 OKR).
Consideration: surface recommended commitment size in Console based on trailing 3-month rolling median usage.
Future: explore committed burst credits that allow temporary headroom without immediate overage billing.
